title: Persistence: The Sustained Effort Necessary to Induce Faith
coreMove: Persistence grows when a burning aim gets a plan in motion, a closed door to discouragement, and allies who keep temporary defeat from voting.

exampleSpecs.stakes: A returned envelope can turn a definite purpose into embarrassment unless the next action is already planned.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Fannie Hurst's years of rejection to show persistence as ordinary continuation.

exampleSpecs.audience: performers whose confidence drops before public exposure
exampleSpecs.stakes: A missed note can become either a practice cue or a reason to quit before the audience hears the work.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Kate Smith and radio to show unseen repetition before opportunity.

exampleSpecs.stakes: A failed launch can tempt the team to abandon the purpose or repeat a plan that evidence has already weakened.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the four steps to distinguish persistence in purpose from blind loyalty to a plan.

exampleSpecs.audience: team leads trying to make follow-through structural
exampleSpecs.stakes: Morale is low enough that private willpower will not carry the turnaround alone.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Make the four-step method visible as a structure, not a mood.

exampleSpecs.audience: writers who let social embarrassment stop a live project
exampleSpecs.stakes: Fear of criticism can end the work before technical weakness gets repaired.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Fannie Hurst to separate useful criticism from discouragement.

exampleSpecs.audience: performers waiting for a break without building repetition
exampleSpecs.stakes: Opportunity may arrive before the habit is ready to meet it.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Kate Smith to connect persistence with ability developed before the audience appears.
